subject: Web Development
title: The Semantic Web Revived
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Semantic Web Revived usable.

hook.text: Tim Berners-Lee dreamed of a web that machines could understand. It mostly didn't happen.

buildup.text: The semantic web required structured data everywhere. Most developers didn't bother.

discovery.text: Large language models now extract meaning from unstructured text — no special markup needed.

twist.text: AI achieved what XML schemas couldn't: making the web's messy content machine-readable.

climax.text: The semantic web arrived — just not in the format its inventor imagined.

punchline.text: AI reads the web that machines couldn't parse.

quiz.question: Why did the original semantic web idea struggle?
options: Most developers didn't add structured data
